Title: Inclusion and no-false-recording
Statement: any displayed “RECORDED/ACCEPTED” status corresponded to a real log inclusion proof.

Title: No undetected equivocation
Statement: a dishonest log operator cannot show inconsistent histories to different audiences without fork evidence.

Title: Election parameter immutability (EPB)
Statement: ballot definitions and critical policies were committed and witnessed before voting.

Title: Results publication integrity + audience parity
Statement: published results objects are content-addressed and consistent across mirrors/audiences.

Title: Dispute-ready evidence bundles
Statement: evidence bundles are immutable, signed, and interpretable under a stated contract.

Title: Canonical evidence packet exists and is verifiable offline
Statement: For each election context, there exists at least one public evidence packet (content-addressed) containing the signed bundle manifest and all referenced artifacts/envelopes such that an independent verifier can validate integrity without network access.
Notes: This is a meta-interface obligation: it prevents format drift and selective disclosure via awkward packaging.

Title: Coverage accounting is published and auditable
Statement: Monitors/watchers publish a signed coverage report for each window, including deterministic sampling inputs, target definitions, and suppression metrics, so selective blindness and challenge grinding become measurable.
Notes: Start with toy metrics; evolve as deployment experience accumulates.

Title: Offline-verifiable evidence packets (canonical envelopes)
Statement: public evidence packets can be verified offline: content-addressed objects match digests; EvidenceEnvelopes bind payloads via RFC8785-JCS payload_digest and tbs_digest; missing objects are detectable; required receipt/gossip attachments are present (or provably missing) per-kind.
Notes: Prevents format drift and supports mirroring under selective disclosure. Adds standardized receipt + gossip attachments for anti-suppression.

Title: Receipted + gossiped publication (anti selective disclosure)
Statement: For core evidence kinds, publication includes a transparency receipt and a gossip summary attachment (per registry); missing attachments are detectable and mirrorable.
Notes: Hardens the verification ecosystem against suppression and split-view targeting by making bad news portable.

Title: Publication contract + portable breach proofs
Statement: A PublicationContract defining per-kind deadlines is published early; missed deadlines are recorded as PublicationSuppressionReports that are themselves receipted + gossiped per registry.
Notes: Turns deadline promises into auditable, portable objects (anti selective delay).

Title: Public notices are verifiable, receipted, and gossiped
Statement: Operational public communications (status/incident/corrections) are published as content-addressed PublicNotice envelopes, and (per registry) include receipt + gossip attachments so selective omission and later dispute are provable.
Notes: Treat communications as evidence objects; corrections must link to prior notices.

Title: Publication compliance coverage is computed and published
Statement: Given a PublicationContract, issuers publish receipted+gossiped TriggerEvents; independent watchers compute and publish PublicationCoverageReports that quantify on-time publication and highlight missed deadlines (including public notices); and watchers publish receipted+gossiped LivenessBeacons capturing reachability/observed digests for the public pointer surfaces so missingness is harder to bury.
Notes: Treat TriggerEvents as the portable anchors that make deadline checks reproducible.

Title: Witness set transparency + change control
Statement: Witness set membership and policy changes are published as receipted+gossiped evidence objects before they take effect; changes bind to an explicit checkpoint boundary so independent verifiers can reconstruct the applicable witness set for any disputed checkpoint.
Notes: This is the “verification ecosystem governance” surface: if witness membership drifts or is selectively disclosed, split-view defenses become political instead of technical.

Title: Receipt UX non-lying rule
Statement: User-facing receipt/status UX MUST NOT imply RECORDED/FINAL/TALLIED unless the corresponding evidence is present in the voter's receipt bundle; anything below RECORDED must be presented as NOT RECORDED (optionally with a short-lived PENDING pre-state plus explicit deadline).
Notes: This is the UX form of “loud failure”: a missing inclusion proof should not become a silent legitimacy trap.

Title: Policy-profile publication for verifier comparability
Statement: Publishable verifier packet reports MUST pin the evaluated policy profile via policy_profile_sha256 and SHOULD ship the profile's RFC8785-JCS canonical bytes as a content-addressed object when emitting a report packet.
Notes: Treat the policy profile as a compact public-surface artifact; keep it stable and cite it by digest.

Title: Anti-grinding challenge coverage
Statement: monitors/watchers could not cherry-pick easy challenges; challenges follow a public schedule.

Title: Suppression proof
Statement: non-response/missed deadlines produce signed suppression artifacts.

Title: Monitor accountability
Statement: monitors’ behavior is itself auditable (watchers inspecting monitors).

Title: Device state attestability
Statement: devices were in an expected state when used (attestation evidence + reference values).

Title: Provenance chain completeness
Statement: firmware and device identity trace back through signed supply-chain statements.

Title: Endorsement + reference-value transparency
Statement: endorsements, reference values, and verifier policy are publicly auditable and split-world resistant (anti-capture).

Title: Auditable software build provenance (SLSA/in-toto)
Statement: software (firmware + verifier + results/reporting stack) is shipped with verifiable build provenance bound to artifacts, enabling reproducibility and forensic audit.
Notes: Start with verifier + results/reporting toolchain; expand to device firmware.

Title: Endorsement/reference updates are transparent, gossiped, and revocable
Statement: Endorsement and reference value registries provide inclusion/consistency proofs, publish within a bounded delay, support revocations, and enable gossip/witnessing to detect split-view behavior.
Notes: Modeled on CT-style MMD and SCITT receipts; exact governance body is out of scope, but evidence rules are in scope.

Title: External challenge / spec correction loop
Statement: Credible external critique or discovered substantive errors trigger a recorded response (ADR + bounded response note) and a shipped regression vector; no silent patching.
Notes: Treat internal coherence as insufficient; prefer independent implementations + test vectors.

Title: ENR content addressing and reproducibility closure
Statement: Every pilot ENR artifact used for public claims must bind UI/API/export bytes to content-addressed payloads and a verifier-reproducible release package.
Notes: No ENR public claim without digest-pinned payloads and a reproducibility report.

Title: Audience parity detection and split-view closure
Statement: Public status, ENR, notice, and correction surfaces must be sampled from multiple perspectives and emit bounded parity snapshots when divergent content is observed.
Notes: Treat parity failure as evidence, not as a narrative conclusion.

Title: Ballot-definition chain and canary binding closure
Statement: Ballot definitions, style files, and public presentation paths must be chained to published hashes, reference values, and canary checks that catch mismatched voter-facing renderings.
Notes: The example is synthetic; live pilots must replace all placeholder digests with jurisdiction artifacts.

Title: Dispute-ready chain of custody and retention closure
Statement: Dispute packets must preserve signed envelopes, manifest digests, timestamps, retention decisions, and public summaries sufficient for later observer or court review.
Notes: Does not make a legal-admissibility claim without a jurisdiction worksheet.

Title: Availability and missingness corroboration closure
Statement: Unreachability, late publication, and missing required artifacts must produce bounded URPs or missingness records corroborated by independent perspectives and public contracts.
Notes: Missingness is reported as absence of expected evidence, not as fraud proof.

Title: Independent notarization and timestamp anchoring closure
Statement: Key public artifacts must be anchored with receipts, gossip summaries, or independent notarization so backdating, rewrite, and selective disclosure attempts are detectable.
Notes: Receipt semantics remain profile-specific; unqualified “included” claims require profile evidence.

Title: Key management and compromise recovery publication closure
Statement: Key rotations, revocations, and compromise recovery events must be signed, gossiped, timestamped, and tied to an effective checkpoint boundary.
Notes: The synthetic example demonstrates shape only; live pilots need authority-specific key policies.

Title: Verifier diversity and no-monoculture closure
Statement: Track A verification claims require at least two independently operated verifier paths or a public declaration that the verifier surface is monoculture and not yet promotable.
Notes: This closes “one verifier says so” as a Track A public-trust claim.
